newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Brazilian firm asks out of Colombia contract deal.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian firm asks out of Colombia contract deal.

text.p: Brazilian engineering firm Andrade Gutierrez has asked the government to cancel its contract to upgrade a highway just outside the Colombian capital because of guerrilla-related violence, authorities said.
Transportation Minister Carlos Hernan Lopez said the verbal request was made last week. "Their complaint is that they haven't been able to continue working," he told the Radionet news program.
Andrade Gutierrez has been working on the highway, which links Bogota to the eastern plains and the nearby city of Villavicencio, for more than two years.

Spokesmen for the firm could not be reached for immediate comment. But it has suffered several high-profile attacks by leftist Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia FARC rebels operating on the southeastern outskirts of Bogota.
The latest attack came on April 4, when rebels destroyed the company's asphalt plant and torched 16 of its dump trucks.
In other actions attributed to guerrillas, two of the company's engineers were released in exchange for a ransom payment last month after a six-month kidnap ordeal.
The FARC, Colombia's largest and oldest guerrilla group, specializes in kidnappings as well as the protection of rural drug farms and laboratories.

Lopez indicated that there would be no formal response to Andrade Gutierrez unless its request for cancellation of the highway contract were put in writing. He conceded that the company had reason to be concerned about security, however, and said the government would hold talks with military officials "within the next few hours" to discuss the possibility of providing better security for private contractors.
"We've had this same problem on highways all over the country," Lopez said, adding that rebels make frequent prey of private companies to collect extortion money and "war taxes" from them.
